beats.narration_text: Veracite will be a command-line tool that checks each claim in a RAG answer against the passage it cites. For every claim it will record three things: is the citation real, is the passage about the right subject, and does it actually support the claim.

beats.narration_text: RAGAS checks each claim against all the retrieved text pooled together, and gives one faithfulness score. ALCE is a research benchmark on fixed datasets, built for comparing models, not for checking your own app. Neither tells you which citation is wrong, or whether the page is even about the right car. Veracite will. My first experiment: running RAGAS on the Camry case, to see if it catches the wrong car.

beats.narration_text: One rule: Veracite will never pass a claim by default. Missing vehicle metadata becomes "unknown". A judge timeout becomes "unverified". Never "supported".

beats.narration_text: In scope: it runs locally, on recorded traces. Out of scope, on purpose: it will not plug into a live production system, and it will never rewrite or block an answer. First: a test where the Camry case returns mismatch, and the same case without vehicle metadata returns unknown, never match.

beats.narration_text: What could sink it: the judge being wrong in ways I can't see, like a false "supported". So the held-out set never touches prompt tuning, and any verdict from an unmeasured judge gets a warning. The limit: the set will be small, and labeled by me alone.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix. I already build RAG pipelines in Python, and my RideReady repo and its git history show that. What's new is evaluation: splitting claims, LLM judges, and measuring a verifier's own error.
